openDecisions.title: Organization deployments
openDecisions.text: jive provision installs a resource component into the organization's own Convex deployment (app.use in its generated convex.config.ts, then a deploy). Open: how each organization's deployment is created and who holds its deploy key.

openDecisions.title: DNS API shape
options: Declarative: setRecords declares every record one owner (a resource instance) wants in a zone; the connector creates, updates and removes to match, touching only that owner's records, which the component tracks in its own table (recommended).
Imperative: ensureRecord adds one record; removing one is a separate call or left to a person.

packages.name: @jive-sh/server
packages.purpose: Database + credential holder (Convex). Deployed. Extends jive-abstract-backend-convex. People sign in with their jive.sh passkey; every call takes a session token, which a CLI or daemon gets by claiming a sign-in request approved on jive.sh/login. Holds each account's SSH key (ed25519, sealed like connections; built 2026-11-01): ssh:sign takes a session token and the bytes an SSH agent was asked to sign, for git commits and SSH logins alike, and returns the signature. Decided 2026-11-01, Alex: "I think a session should only be obtainable via human passkey, cicd oidc token exchange, or jive mints a token and hands it off to a compute provider running an agent workflow. So three methods and only 2 of them are available via cli". Today: passkey is built (in the browser, and for programs through sign-in requests); the CI/CD OIDC exchange is built (0.5.0, 2026-11-01: pipelineSessions:signIn turns a deploy job's GitHub ID token into a one-hour session for its registered code repository, and packages:provision takes that session token; jive-abstract-library 0.8.0 calls both); minting for a compute provider is not built and depends on the compute resource kind. A test fails if any other code opens a session. Decided 2026-11-01, Alex (his idea: "both the ssh thing and the passkey thing could go into a convex component"): one Convex component installed in @jive-sh/server holds each account's private keys sealed in its own tables (ed25519 for SSH signing, P-256 for passkeys) and signs from a Node action given a session token; the server's SSH keys move into it, and @jive-sh/cloud-sk is retired once it lands. Being built by Grok's thread

packages.name: @jive-sh/jive
packages.purpose: The jive CLI + the shared CI/CD pipeline. Replaces @ozyman42/ozy-cli (0.3.0, 2026-11-01): jive login (passkey sign-in request, which also fetches the account's public key) and jive login --cicd (GitHub OIDC for a pipeline session) are the only ways to a session; jive load registers the account key on GitHub and configures the repo and its submodules; jive git setup was removed in 0.3.0 (Alex, 2026-11-01: "git setup probably goes away honestly"), and the code-repository connector is to derive each package's git URL; jive-signing-agent holds no key and forwards each sign request to @jive-sh/server ssh:sign; jive daemons, jive upgrade. Next: jive provision <kind> <instance> (e.g. connector-package-registry @jive-sh/server-client), the organization picking the implementation, which the deploy hook will run after jive login --cicd

packages.name: jive-abstract-resource
packages.purpose: Defines a kind of resource an organization owns, as a Convex component. Decided 2026-11-01: each resource kind is a connector abstract with a standard "make sure this exists" call; an implementation is a library shipping the component; instances are declared in the package's jive block and held as records in that component; jive provision lists resource packages by the jive-resource- prefix. Decided 2026-11-01, Alex: "We have a deploy hook in CI. That should do a `jive login --cicd` then `jive provision` for a given resource", and "it should probably only be provisioning the abstract. so `jive provision connector-package-registry` and then it talks to the jive org which should have one impl configured". So a caller names the resource kind and the instance; each organization configures exactly one implementation per kind; this generic call replaces packages:provision on @jive-sh/server
